key_insights: Rally on 11/11 was narrow and semis-led: SOX +5.5%, ARM +12%, MU +12%, while MSFT, META and AMZN closed lower. The broader tech complex held up despite heavy market cap concentration in Nvidia and increasingly idiosyncratic Nvidia problems.
Governance issues at Nvidia are described as forcing a significant rebalancing of capital. NVDA dropped roughly 9% overnight, weighing on the Asia tech tape.
Retail Favorites basket (GSXURFAV) rose +495bps, its 3rd best day in three years. Three sub-$4 stocks accounted for 32% of US tape volume.
Vol complex has largely reset: the SPX vol curve un-inverted, dealer skew flattened, and systematic L/S managers had their best two-day return in nearly three years (+2.15%).

The open question is whether the bid is a mechanical result of lower positioning and short covering or the start of something more durable. Breadth remains narrow, but absorbing this much Nvidia-specific pressure without broader capitulation is noteworthy.

Iran: headlines conflict. Reports of a contentious Netanyahu-Trump call over renewed strikes (disputed by Netanyahu's office), Vance reportedly exploring direct talks that Tehran has resisted, and Iranian officials saying Washington signaled roughly a 2-week window before deciding on further military action. A third US carrier group is heading to the region, possibly arriving mid-month, though it may relieve an existing deployment. Desk has low conviction on direction.

Russia/Ukraine: Polymarket pricing for a ceasefire by December has fallen toward 10%, with March around 25%. Abu Dhabi talks produced agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange but little progress on territorial and security questions. Progress is plausible in 2027 but hard to argue for within two months.

AI hardware: desk separates fundamental compute demand from valuation multiples. Hyperscalers are best positioned given balance sheet capacity and contracted infrastructure. Four overhangs: higher cost of capital, power/permitting constraints, supply/demand balance entering 2028, and monetization velocity relative to capex. Expects episodic, high-beta trading rallies rather than buy-and-hold, with strong micro results coexisting with multiple compression.

Risk view: this could be a bear market rally. A durable breakout likely needs lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership. Candidate groups outside AI infrastructure are hyperscalers, transports, cyclicals and aerospace, and defense looks washed out. These are hard to sustain against an aggressive hiking cycle and high oil. Desk expects chop rather than breakout absent relief, though low positioning and high vol are short-term tailwinds.
